2010_000_011910org_regmtg.paragraph: Combined Organizational Meeting (7:00 p.m.) and Regular Meeting (7:30 p.m.) of the Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, January 19, 2010, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Organizational business appointed Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, as Treasurer for the 2010 calendar year and named Shelly Carrier to post meeting notices. Most of the packet is the Treasurer's Report for November and December 2009 — total disbursements of $10,563,664.79 and $7,407,103.51 — with fiscal year 2010 budget reports; the sharpest action item is a resolution that the district will NOT enter a Service Consolidation Plan agreement with the Michigan Department of Education under MCL 388.1611D(2).

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, Organizational Meeting 7:00 p.m. and Regular Meeting 7:30 p.m., Tuesday, January 19, 2010, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098.

**Organizational actions**
Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer of the Board for the 2010 calendar year; the Superintendent of Schools continued as Deputy Secretary; Shelly Carrier, Secretary to the Superintendent, designated to post notices of meetings; the meeting schedule for the 2010 calendar year adopted.

**Recognitions**
111 senior scholar athletes from fall sports (3.5 cumulative GPA while participating), from Athens and Troy High Schools; seven all-state fall athletes, all Troy High (Michael Atchoo, Sean Cunningham, Brett Forman, Nathan Hicklin, Lee Keating, Michelle Moriset, Susan Stuecheli); and a Board recognition slide show by Boulan Park Middle School students.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the December 1, 2009 meeting, December 8, 2009 workshop, January 6, 2010 special meeting, January 11, 2010 special meeting and January 11, 2010 workshop, plus the Treasurer's Report for November and December 2009. Actions recorded there include Motion 09-056 awarding Boulan Park media center furniture to Office Express for $23,417.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; Motion 10-058, carried 5-2, authorizing a Race to the Top letter of intent to the Oakland Intermediate School District Superintendent; and Motion 10-059, an amended Race to the Top Memorandum of Understanding resolution that failed 2-4 with Mrs. Fleming absent.

2010_000_011910org_regmtg.verbose:
Packet for the Troy School District Board of Education combined Organizational Meeting (7:00 p.m.) and Regular Meeting (7:30 p.m.) of Tuesday, January 19, 2010 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; board offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Organizational meeting.** Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer of the Board for the 2010 calendar year; the Superintendent continued as Deputy Secretary; Shelly Carrier designated to post notices of meetings; and the 2010 calendar-year meeting schedule adopted.

**Recognitions.** 111 senior scholar athletes from fall sports, each maintaining a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating, from Athens High School and Troy High School. Seven all-state fall athletes, all Troy High: Michael Atchoo (cross country; State Champ 2009 XC and 1600 track, 15:22; Division 1 mile, 4:07), Sean Cunningham and Nathan Hicklin (soccer), Brett Forman and Lee Keating (tennis), Michelle Moriset (cross country) and Susan Stuecheli (volleyball).

**Consent agenda (item 5).** Minutes of the December 1 and December 8, 2009 meetings and the January 6 and January 11, 2010 special meeting and workshop, plus the Treasurer's Report for November and December 2009.

**December 2009 minutes.** The December 1 meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Underwood; present Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Philippart, absent Miletti and Pochodylo. Kathleen Davisson was recognized as the 2009 winner of the Reading Recovery Council of Michigan Award, and Motion 09-055 approved the November 17, 2009 minutes, Ayes 5, Nays 0. Motion 09-056 awarded the Boulan Park Middle School media center furniture bid to Office Express for $23,417.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; Motion 09-057 set a special workshop for January 12, 2010. Dr. Fowler relayed word from lobbyist Judy Allen that legislators were unlikely to take up the $127 per pupil reduction or 20j funding before the first of the year, and described a December 9, 2009 Lansing trip to meet Representative Marty Knollenberg and Senator John Pappageorge. The December 8 workshop covered an Enviro-Clean update, alternative revenue development, a mid-year budget update and reductions, consolidation agreements and robo calls.

**Race to the Top actions.** On January 6, 2010, Motion 10-058 authorized the Board President and Superintendent to sign a Message of Intent letter to the Oakland Intermediate School District Superintendent regarding the Michigan Participating LEA/ISD Memorandum of Understanding; carried 5-2, Hauff and Underwood voting no. On January 11, 2010, Motion 10-059 offered an amended resolution reciting the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009's $4.35 billion Race to the Top Fund, Michigan's lack of a conforming final statewide plan, State Superintendent Michael Flanagan's written assurance that districts could rescind, and a deadline moved from January 7 to January 12, 2010. It rejected the state's proposed Section III paragraphs III(6) and III(7) and replaced Section V with language preserving the right to rescind and disclaiming any waiver of rights under the Headlee Amendment (Article 9, Section 29 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963). Roll call: Philippart and Miletti yes; Pochodylo, Underwood, Edmunds and Hauff no; Fleming absent — Yes 2, No 4, and the resolution failed. Motion 10-060 canceled the January 12, 2010 workshop, Yes 6, No 0.

**Item 6.A, personnel.** The collective bargaining agreement with TESPA/MEA/NEA — representing maintenance, para-educator and bilingual/ESL para-educator staff — expires June 30, 2010. The resolution appoints Jasen Witt as chief spokesperson with team members Michael Adamczyk, Richard Machesky, Mondo Belardi, Gary Wood, Linda Hannon and Bonnie Lobert.

**Item 7.A, enrollment projections.** Dr. Don Van Den Berghe, principal of Wass Elementary School, presents the annual enrollment projections report.

**Item 7.B, NASA downlink.** Troy was selected as Michigan's only community, and one of only six in the nation, to host a live downlink with International Space Station crew members, presented by Jennifer Gottlieb, Science and Math Coordinator. It is set for February 1 in the Athens High School Auditorium, streaming live district-wide, with 15 to 20 students questioning the Expedition 22 crew: Commander Jeffrey Williams and Flight Engineers T.J. Creamer, Soichi Noguchi, Maxim Suraev and Oleg Kotov. Smith students won the WING (What if No Gravity) competition and Athens AP Physics groups were NASA DIME Tier 2 winners, both sending experiments to the NASA Glenn Research Center. A "Troy Travels to Space" community evening was tentatively set for February 1, 2010, 6:30 to 8:00 p.m., in the Athens High School Main Gym.

**Item 7.C, Great Start Readiness.** Resolution certifying participation in the 2009-2010 Great Start Readiness State Aid program under Sections 32d and 37 through 40 and Section 38 of the State School Aid Act. The district is eligible for an allocation of $54,400 for fiscal year 2009-2010 for a school readiness program for 16 children. It will not provide full-day preschool ($-0- at the approved per-capita allowance of $6,600) or comprehensive parent involvement programs ($-0-), but will provide half-day preschool for 16 eligible four-year-olds using $54,400 at the approved per-capita allowance of $3,400. Adopted this 19th day of January 2010.

**Items 7.D and 7.E, Schools of Choice.** Under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, the Board will accept applications for a limited Schools of Choice program for the 2010-2011 school year for nonresident kindergarten and first-grade students within Oakland County, and for students attending a district in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries.

**Item 8.A, consolidation of services.** MCL 388.1611D(2) requires a district to enter an agreement with the Michigan Department of Education no later than February 1, 2010 if it intends to apply the $165 per pupil deduction in 2009-10 State School Aid revenue against an unprotected categorical other than Section 22b. Citing savings already achieved through cooperative purchasing and service consolidation, the resolution states that the Troy School District will NOT enter into such an agreement to develop a Service Consolidation Plan.

**Item 8.B, media center books.** Bids for a three-year contract to supply media center books district-wide were opened July 15, 2009; 11 firms were invited, eight responded, one a "No Bid." Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, recommended the award in a January 14, 2010 memo to Michael Adamczyk; Scott Bryan, Director of Technology, wrote January 7, 2010 that International Academy East had ordered books to complete its library startup. The resolution awards the bid to Follett for $36,157.54 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, covering 1,408 books and 1 audio-visual title plus processing. Signed Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D., Superintendent of Schools.
